exercises: Pick any claim in this guide, follow its source link, and confirm the source actually says what the claim says.
Write the shelf label for three substance claims you hear this week: documented, theoretical, or unstudied — and say why.
Open MCL 257.625 on legislature.mi.gov and write down, in your own words, exactly what subsection (8) criminalizes.
Find the Clean Slate / MC 228 pathway in this guide and name one waiting period for one type of drug conviction.

intermediate.label: Intermediate 📈 · Shelf 2 — Theoretical
intermediate.tagline: SHELF 2 OF 3 — THEORETICAL: mechanism-reasoned expectations, labeled as theory every time. Plausible is not documented — no human co-use trial exists for any pairing in this guide.
goals: Tell a theoretical claim from a documented one using the lane status labels
Explain dual pressor stacking and why it is expected but untested
Place serotonin syndrome from psilocybin + cocaine on the correct shelf
Spot animal and in-vitro data being extrapolated to humans
State a theory in the reserved language the corpus uses

concepts.title: How to read a theoretical claim
concepts.text:
Theoretical is not an insult and not a green light. Here it means: the mechanism is real chemistry or real physiology, the conclusion is reasoned from it, and no human co-use trial measured the result.

Three tells that you are standing on this shelf:
- The lane status says MIXED, THEORETICAL, or SPECULATIVE.
- The claim rests on animal, in-vitro, or single-substance data extrapolated to a combination.
- Words like expected, plausible, likely or inferred are doing the work a study would normally do.

Speech rules for this shelf: say “pharmacologically expected, never tested in humans” — not “this happens.” Reserve “documented” for a citation about the combination itself. Serotonin syndrome from psilocybin + cocaine is the textbook case: plausible mechanism, but every documented serotonin-toxicity case involves an MAOI or a serotonergic medication.

⚠ Shelf 2 is not safety. Absence of evidence for a dangerous mechanism is not evidence of absence — it is a reason for care, never a reason for confidence.

concepts.title: Lane 2 — the theory shelf (2 of 14 findings)
concepts.text:
Mechanism-reasoned, never measured in a human co-use trial:
- [L2] DOCUMENTED: psilocin is eliminated mainly by glucuronidation (UGT1A9 liver, UGT1A10 intestine; ~20% of dose as psilocin-O-glucuronide in 24h) and MAO-A-driven oxidation to 4-HIAA (~33% of dose); CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolize psilocin in vitro but are minor in vivo, and CYP2D6 GENOTYPE DID NOT CHANGE psilocin plasma exposure in humans (unlike LSD/MDMA). THEORETICAL ONLY: ethanol is metabolized by alcohol/aldehyde dehydrogenase (ADH/ALDH), which may also participate in psilocin's 4-HIA -> 4-HIAA/4-HTP step - competition/induction with ethanol is untested; NO published ethanol-psilocybin pharmacokinetic interaction study was located. — (VERIFIED (psilocin metabolism); ethanol PK competition UNVERIFIED/theoretical) Source: Front Pharmacol 2024;15:1391689; systematic review [PMC11762572](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11762572/)
- [L2] KNOWN: psilocin binds 5-HT2A (Ki ~41 nM), 5-HT1A (~128 nM), 5-HT2C (~136 nM) and moderately inhibits SERT; ethanol acts as GABA-A positive modulator and NMDA antagonist (NIAAA). Animal literature cited within Barrett 2000: drugs acting at 5-HT1/5-HT2 receptors alter ethanol intake and discriminative-stimulus effects in rats. SPECULATED: direct human co-ingestion receptor-level pharmacodynamics (5-HT2A x GABA/NMDA) have not been studied; any detailed mechanism of the subjective interaction 'must remain largely speculative' (Barrett et al.'s own words). — (VERIFIED (separate pharmacologies); human co-ingestion mechanism SPECULATIVE) Source: Front Pharmacol 2024;15:1391689 (binding data); NIAAA Alcohol and the Brain; [PMID 12404626](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12404626/) (rat-literature citation and author caution)

concepts.title: Lane 5 — the theory shelf (6 of 15 findings)
concepts.text:
Expected physiology, no human combination data:
- [L5] In vitro, recombinant CYP2D6 metabolized nearly 100% of psilocin (quinidine-inhibitable) and CYP3A4 ~40%, but in the human study CYP2D6 genotype did NOT change psilocin plasma exposure; systematic reviews still list CYP2D6/CYP3A4 as theoretical drug-interaction handles while documenting glucuronidation + MAO-A as the dominant in-vivo routes. — So what: Any claim that a co-used drug 'competes for psilocin's CYP2D6 metabolism' is theoretical, not documented — flag it as such in education. — (MIXED — in-vitro enzyme data verified; human clinical relevance of CYP2D6 variation NOT demonstrated) Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC11089204](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11089204/)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC11089204](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11089204/)); [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38741590](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38741590); [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12030428](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12030428/)/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12030428](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12030428/)/)
- [L5] Classic psychedelics produce dose-dependent transient heart-rate and blood-pressure increases (5-HT2A-related sympathomimetic effect); cocaine adds direct sympathetic stimulation and vasoconstriction, so tachycardia/hypertension stacking is physiologically expected — but no dedicated human co-use trial exists. — So what: Two independent pressor/tachycardic mechanisms stack; harm-reduction literature treats stimulant x psychedelic as a high-risk pairing on this basis. — (MIXED — individual drug effects verified; the combined effect is pharmacologically inferred, untested) Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC10661823](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10661823/)/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC10661823](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10661823/)/); [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430769](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430769); [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39042251](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39042251)
- [L5] Psilocin is a partial 5-HT2A agonist (~16% of serotonin's signaling efficacy) that does not raise intrasynaptic 5-HT, which is why severe serotonin toxicity from psilocybin alone is rare; documented ST cases involve serotonergic medication combos (e.g., trazodone added to venlafaxine/bupropion plus frequent psilocybin use; scoping review found antidepressant+psilocybin generally showed no robust ST signal). Cocaine raises synaptic serotonin via SERT blockade, making ST mechanistically plausible — but NO documented psilocybin+cocaine serotonin-syndrome case was located. — So what: Frame serotonin syndrome with cocaine+psilocybin as a plausible-but-unproven mechanism, reserving 'documented' for MAOI and serotonergic-drug combinations. — (MIXED — psilocin pharmacology and medication cases VERIFIED; cocaine-combination ST risk UNVERIFIED/theoretical) Source: [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34251464/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34251464/); [https://psychiatrist.com/pcc/psilocybin-development-serotonin-toxicity](https://psychiatrist.com/pcc/psilocybin-development-serotonin-toxicity); [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12572353](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12572353/)/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12572353](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12572353/)/)
- [L5] Ethanol is metabolized by ADH/ALDH (primary) and CYP2E1/catalase (minor), NOT CYP2D6, so 'ethanol competes for psilocin's CYP2D6 clearance' has no supporting literature; the only published mechanism is speculative — ethanol-derived acetaldehyde forming tetrahydroisoquinolines/beta-carbolines with MAO-inhibiting properties, proposed to raise mushroom toxicity (van Amsterdam 2011). No study documents ethanol altering psilocybin/psilocin pharmacokinetics, and no human PK study of oral freebase psilocin with ethanol exists. — So what: Do not present alcohol-psilocin CYP competition as fact — the honest position is 'no controlled data; one speculative MAO-inhibition hypothesis.' — (UNVERIFIED (theoretical) — mechanism is explicitly 'speculated' in the literature) Source: [https://link.springer.com/article/[DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-92392-1_130](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/978-3-030-92392-1_130](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-92392-1_130](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/978-3-030-92392-1_130)); [https://www.niaaa.nih.gov/publications/alcohol-metabolism](https://www.niaaa.nih.gov/publications/alcohol-metabolism); [https://doi.org/[DOI 10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228))
- [L5] Nausea/vomiting and transient tachycardia/hypertension are the most reported physiological psilocybin effects, and both psilocin and alcohol are independently emetogenic (alcohol via gastric irritation and its own effects), so additive GI distress is expected though not specifically quantified in co-use studies; alcohol additionally erodes judgment and set-and-setting during a cognitively altered state — government HR guidance (Ireland HSE) warns mixing mushrooms with alcohol produces 'unpredictable and negative effects.' — So what: Vomiting while heavily intoxicated in either direction raises aspiration/injury risk — a practical harm independent of any PK question. — (MIXED — individual effects VERIFIED; combined nausea amplification UNQUANTIFIED (theoretical)) Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC9353971](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9353971/)/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC9353971](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9353971/)/); [https://www2.hse.ie/living-well/drugs/types/psilocybin/reducing-harm/](https://www2.hse.ie/living-well/drugs/types/psilocybin/reducing-harm/); [https://psychonautwiki.org/wiki/Psilocybin_mushrooms](https://psychonautwiki.org/wiki/Psilocybin_mushrooms)
- [L5] Large interindividual variation in psilocin plasma concentrations after oral psilocybin is documented in human PK studies; CYP2D6 poor/ultrarapid-metabolizer effects on psilocin exposure were NOT observed in the one human genotype analysis (so phenotype claims remain theoretical), while gut-microbiome reviews report in-vitro bacterial strains capable of dephosphorylating psilocybin and propose microbiota composition and gut alkaline-phosphatase activity as sources of response variability — review-level/in-vitro only, not clinical. — So what: Population PK numbers do not transfer to individuals — identical exposure can differ between people, which is itself a co-use risk argument. — (MIXED — PK scatter and in-vitro microbiome findings VERIFIED; clinical impact of CYP2D6 phenotype and microbiome UNPROVEN) Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC11089204](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11089204/)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC11089204](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11089204/)); [https://doi.org/[DOI 10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228](https://doi.org/10.1080/03602532.2016.1278228)); [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40631920](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40631920); [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12151692](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12151692/)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC12151692](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12151692/))

concepts.title: Lane 6 — the theory shelf (3 of 9 findings)
concepts.text:
Theory behind the microdosing risk factors:
- [L6] Physical risk - cardiac: chronic 5-HT2B agonism is a documented theoretical valvulopathy/fibrosis pathway. LSD (Ki 0.98 nM) and psilocin (Ki 4.6 nM) are high-affinity 5-HT2B agonists structurally similar to known valvulopathic drugs (methysergide, pergolide, fenfluramine; chronic MDMA also linked to valve damage). A 2026 systematic review (17 studies) found preclinical and in vitro support for fibrotic signaling under sustained exposure but NO clinical cases of LSD/psilocybin-induced valvulopathy and NO controlled studies in chronic human microdosers. A 2025 mouse study (ACS Pharmacol Transl Sci) found no valvulopathy from chronic microdose LSD, with estimated 5-HT2B occupancy for LSD/psilocybin microdoses ~half that of fenfluramine and cleared by 10h - but authors explicitly state mouse null results do not prove human safety. — So what: Honest framing: risk is theoretical/preclinical, unquantified in humans, but biologically plausible specifically because microdosing is CHRONIC exposure - the exact pattern that caused fenfluramine and pergolide valve disease. Cardiac screening (echo/history of valve disease) is recommended in the literature before long-term regimens; anyone with known valvular disease has no data assuring safety. — (moderate) Source: Rouaud et al. 2024, J Psychopharmacol ([PMID 38214279](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38214279/) / [PMC10944580](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10944580/)); Tagen et al. 2023 review; ACS Pharmacol Transl Sci 2025 ([DOI 10.1021/acsptsci.5c00202](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsptsci.5c00202)); Pharmacopsychiatry 2026 systematic review ([PMID 41643722](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41643722/))
- [L6] Alcohol x microdosing: the liver-enzyme and 'blunted window' mechanisms are THEORETICAL, not documented for this combination. What IS documented: (a) psilocin metabolism runs mainly through glucuronidation (UGT1A9/1A10) plus MAO-A, with CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 contributions - alcohol-induced CYP changes are not a demonstrated psilocin interaction, and psilocin's short half-life (~2-5h) limits interaction windows; (b) survey data document harm-reduction behavior: microdosers commonly report avoiding alcohol on dosing days (Lea 2020), and psychedelic community advice overwhelmingly says don't mix with alcohol (20.8% of first-experience advisers in PMC12648905); (c) the self-medication escalation concern runs in the documented direction the other way - high-dose psilocybin trials for AUD (Bogenschutz 2022 JAMA Psychiatry) show REDUCED heavy drinking days, and survey data show reduced alcohol use after psychedelic experiences (PMC8801670; ~44% of microdosers reporting reduced caffeine/alcohol habits per Anderson 2019 codebook). No study documents alcohol + sub-perceptual dosing as a combination risk pattern; daily drinkers co-using microdoses is unstudied. — So what: Label honestly: 'alcohol blunts/flattens the microdose window via liver enzymes' is folklore-adjacent, not established pharmacology; the defensible education point is that mixing any CNS-active substances during a dosing window confounds self-observation and that co-use with a dependence pattern is a documented red flag for escalating use generally. — (moderate (behavior documented; pharmacology theoretical)) Source: [PMC11089204](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11089204/) psilocin metabolism; Lea et al. 2020 ([DOI 10.1016/j.drugalcdep](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.drugalcdep) in ScienceDirect S095539591930307X); Bogenschutz et al. 2022, JAMA Psychiatry; [PMC12648905](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12648905/) first-experience harm reduction survey; [PMC8801670](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8801670/) health behavior change review
- [L6] SSRI/medication context: serotonin syndrome from psilocybin + SSRI/SNRI is largely theoretical - a 2025 scoping review (PMC12572353) found the combination is NOT reliably associated with serotonin toxicity, and the first published co-medication case report (duloxetine + vortioxetine + 25mg psilocybin, PMC11289768) was well tolerated with no cardiovascular events. The dominant documented interaction is BLUNTING (SSRI downregulates 5-HT2A; Becker 2022 showed escitalopram pretreatment significantly reduced psilocybin subjective effects), which for microdosing means plausibly weaker or absent subjective signal. Harder contraindications documented in trial protocols: lithium and MAOIs (genuine toxicity concerns), plus antipsychotics attenuating effects via 5-HT2A antagonism. Fluvoxamine (strong CYP1A2/CYP2D6 inhibitor) is a pharmacokinetic wildcard noted in the literature. — So what: For educators: never advise anyone to stop prescribed antidepressants to 'make microdosing work' - discontinuation syndrome is documented and can be severe; med changes are a prescriber conversation. — (high) Source: [PMC12572353](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12572353/) scoping review; [PMC11289768](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11289768/)/Front Psychiatry 2024 case report; Becker et al. 2022, Neuropsychopharmacology; [PMC12030428](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12030428/) psilocybin PK systematic review

concepts.title: Ch. 7 — The theorized hazards of the proposed mixture
concepts.text:
Ch. 7 split its hazards the same way this guide does. These are mechanism-reasoned, not measured — every one of them is labeled theory on purpose.

Theorized (mechanism-reasoned, labeled as such):
- Sip-gradient hazard: solids settle and concentration stratifies, so two people — or one person twice — can drink “the same pour” and get very different alkaloid amounts. Mechanistic inference from non-uniformity plus gravity; untested as stated.
- The stacking loop, bottled: alcohol softens comedowns, stimulants cancel ethanol drowsiness while blood alcohol climbs, and a psychedelic dims the felt alcohol effect — a mixture pre-combines all three stop-signal cancellers, so a person's felt sense of dose is untrustworthy by design of the preparation.
- Dual pressor stacking: psilocin's sympathomimetic action plus cocaine's reuptake blockade and vasoconstriction means two independent tachycardia / hypertension systems, expected to add strain — never human-tested, with ethanol's vasodilation swings on top of an unstudied triple interaction.
- Serotonin-syndrome position: from psilocin + cocaine this stays theoretical — no documented case, partial agonist at roughly 16% efficacy. Reserved language only.

examples.title: “It's documented that mixing causes serotonin syndrome”
examples.scenario: A health post warns that psilocybin plus cocaine reliably produces serotonin syndrome, citing case reports.
examples.outcome: The documented serotonin-toxicity cases involve MAOIs and serotonergic medications — not this combination. Psilocin is a partial 5-HT2A agonist at roughly 16% of serotonin's signaling efficacy and does not raise intrasynaptic serotonin. The honest sentence is: plausible mechanism, no documented case. Overstating it burns credibility the community needs for claims that are real.

examples.title: “The enzyme studies prove alcohol blocks psilocin clearance”
examples.scenario: Someone quotes an in-vitro CYP2D6 result as settled proof that alcohol and psilocin compete for metabolism.
examples.outcome: Two lanes disagree with them. In vitro, CYP2D6 metabolizes nearly 100% of psilocin — but in the human genotype study CYP2D6 phenotype did not change psilocin exposure. And ethanol runs ADH/ALDH plus CYP2E1, not CYP2D6: the only published competition mechanism is explicitly speculative. Label it theoretical and move on.

examples.title: “Rats proved alcohol blunts the psychedelic”
examples.outcome: Alcohol-dependent rats do show blunted psilocybin default-mode-network effects — that is real preclinical work. Human blunting data are essentially absent; Barrett 2000 gives retrospective self-report only. Species translation is an inference, so the claim stays on this shelf with its animal origin stated.
examples.scenario: A forum poster upgrades a rat neuroscience finding into a human guarantee in either direction.

pitfalls: MYTH: “Ethanol preserves psilocybin, so a bottle keeps it fine.” The preservation claim is UNVERIFIED with no located supporting study — psilocin oxidizes to blue quinoid oligomers and is unstable even in whole blood.
Treating “pharmacologically expected” as if it were measured: expected stacking, expected nausea amplification and expected sip-gradient differences all still lack a human number.
Quote the origin with the claim: in-vitro, animal, retrospective and expert-consensus ratings are four different evidence types, and none of them is a controlled human co-use trial.
A theory can be right and still be unproven — and a theory can be wrong. Both outcomes are why the shelf exists.
exercises: Find three findings on this shelf and underline the exact word that marks them as theory (expected, plausible, speculative, inferred).
Rewrite one theoretical claim in the reserved language: “pharmacologically expected, never tested in humans.”
Take a claim you have heard about mixing alcohol with psychedelics and ask: is the source human, animal, or in-vitro? Label the shelf it belongs on.
Explain to someone, in two sentences, why a plausible mechanism does not justify either panic or comfort.

advanced.label: Advanced 🚀 · Shelf 3 — Unstudied
advanced.tagline: SHELF 3 OF 3 — UNSTUDIED: where the data does not exist. This shelf is short on purpose — and it carries every UNVERIFIED flag the lanes refused to upgrade, 11 in the Michigan legal lane alone.
goals: Say plainly which combinations have never been studied in humans
Read the UNVERIFIED flag ledger without laundering a flag into a fact
Use the placebo problem to judge any microdosing claim you meet
Apply the three-question screen and the single-substance pattern
Handle an unknown in community education without overclaiming either way

concepts.title: Why this shelf is short — the honest unknown
concepts.text:
This shelf is deliberately thin, and its thinness is the finding.

No controlled human trial has co-administered alcohol with cocaine, psilocybin, or cannabis on purpose; no human pharmacokinetic study exists for psilocybin × ethanol or for cocaine × psilocin; and no study of any triple mixture of the kind the community asked about exists anywhere. Every “it feels smoother” anecdote in circulation rides on zero controlled data.

What lives here:
- Findings whose primary status is UNSTUDIED.
- The UNVERIFIED flag ledger — every open question the lanes refused to upgrade: 2 in lane 1, 8 in lane 2, 5 in lane 3, 11 in lane 4, 4 in lane 6.
- The rules for acting on an unknown.

⚠ An UNVERIFIED flag is not a soft fact. It means the claim was checked and the check did not come back clean — secondary source only, conflicting sources, or no source located. Carry the flag forward exactly as written; do not launder it into a fact by repeating it confidently.

concepts.title: Findings the lanes marked UNSTUDIED (2)
concepts.text:
No data exists — the flag rides with the claim:
- [L5] Alcohol co-use is common: 1,234 of 2,841 psychedelic-using drinkers in the 2024 National Survey Investigating Hallucinogenic Trends reported past-year psilocybin+alcohol co-use, and 19% of people reporting challenging psilocybin experiences had used alcohol (Carbonaro 2016); yet Johns Hopkins' harm-reduction guide notes a lack of studies on concurrent alcohol-psilocybin use, judging pharmacologic synergy unlikely while flagging alcohol-impaired judgment as the behavioral risk. — So what: Widespread co-use with zero controlled interaction data — the documented risk is behavioral (judgment, set-and-setting), not a proven PK interaction. — (VERIFIED (prevalence and evidence-gap statements); the interaction itself is UNSTUDIED) Source: [https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/[DOI 10.1177/00220426261466154](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/00220426261466154](https://doi.org/10.1177/00220426261466154](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/00220426261466154)); [https://www.hopkinsguides.com/hopkins/view/Johns_Hopkins_Psychiatry_Guide/787494/all/Harm_Reduction_and_Safety_in_Recreational_Psychedelic_Use%C2%A0](https://www.hopkinsguides.com/hopkins/view/Johns_Hopkins_Psychiatry_Guide/787494/all/Harm_Reduction_and_Safety_in_Recreational_Psychedelic_Use%C2%A0); [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC9353971](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9353971/)/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/[PMC9353971](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9353971/)/)
- [L6] Physical risk - stimulant stacking: mostly UNSTUDIED. Survey data document the behavior exists: 6.4% of microdosers reported prescription psychostimulants (methylphenidate/amphetamine-based), and microdosers were ~5x more likely than non-microdosers to report recent recreational substance use including stimulants and MDMA. Naturalistic ADHD studies document microdosers self-medicating ADHD and some discontinuing prescribed ADHD meds without medical supervision. No controlled study has examined psilocybin/LSD microdose + stimulant co-use; serotonergic psychedelic + dopaminergic/noradrenergic stimulant cardiovascular load (heart rate/BP elevation on both sides) is an untested combination. — So what: Flag as UNVERIFIED territory: additive cardiovascular stimulation and unsupervised discontinuation of prescribed ADHD medication are the concrete risks educators should name. — (moderate (behavior documented; interaction unstudied)) Source: Rosenbaum et al. 2020 ([PMID 32108529](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32108529/)); [PMC12244228](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12244228/) (prospective ADHD microdosing study); [PMC10966614](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10966614/) (microdosing vs ADHD medication comparison)

concepts.title: Ch. 7 — Unstudied: what nobody has measured
concepts.text:
For the tincture question specifically, the unstudied list is total:
- No human pharmacokinetic study of psilocybin × ethanol, and none of cocaine × psilocin.
- No study of any triple co-use mixture of this kind.
- No dedicated human sublingual PK study for psilocybin at all — clinical dosing is oral, and transmucosal behavior is extrapolated from other drugs.
- No validated shelf-life or stability data for such a mixture, and no literature supporting ethanol as a psilocin preservative.
- Pour-to-pour uniformity: theorized to stratify, never tested — because testing it would be a protocol, which this guide does not do.

The honest sentence for every line above: nobody knows, and anyone selling confidence here is working from nothing.

⚠ “No study exists” is not permission. It is the reason the default answer stays no.

concepts.title: UNVERIFIED flag ledger — Lanes 1 and 2 — the open questions (10 flags)
concepts.text:
These are not findings. They are claims the lanes checked and refused to upgrade — printed exactly as recorded, flags and all.

Flag ledger:
- UNVERIFIED — LANE1: urine windows (48-72h / 5-14d) — secondary sources only
- UNVERIFIED — LANE1: seizure-risk association — secondary only (keep Pennings aggression line as supported).
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Quantitative ethanol-vs-water psilocybin extraction efficiency (no located study; direction of solubility is documented)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Ethanol as an effective psilocin preservative (not validated; degradation chemistry argues against)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Alcohol blunting psilocybin's subjective effects in humans (anecdotal; documented only as rat-model DMN blunting in alcohol dependence)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Nausea/vomiting amplification magnitude for combined co-ingestion (no co-use quantification)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Ethanol ADH/ALDH competition with psilocin's acid-metabolite pathway (theoretical; no PK interaction study)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Blackout rates during alcohol+psilocybin co-use (no psilocybin-specific study)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Alcohol as an HPPD risk factor (not established)
- UNVERIFIED — LANE2: Historical ethanol-based psilocybin preparations (none located; documented traditional preparations are water/food-based)

- UNVERIFIED — LANE3: Exact CRA THC-limit table values (10 mg/serving adult-use edibles; 100 mg max per beverage container) are corroborated by secondary reproductions of the Apr 2025 bulletin; the PDF table itself is an image, so verify against the bulletin before quoting numbers.
- UNVERIFIED — LANE3: Michigan hemp-consumable general-retail THC threshold: secondary sources conflict (some claim a 1.75 mg/serving tier from 2024; others say that rule was deleted before adoption). Verified statutory mechanism only: consumables above the CRA-set THC limit fall under marihuana regulation (MCL 333.27953 as amended by 2021 PA 56 / HB 4517); a federal 0.4 mg/container cap is scheduled to take effect Nov 12, 2026 — treat the hemp-beverage lane as fast-moving and re-verify.
- UNVERIFIED — LANE3: USP cannabis admission year: 1850 (3rd edition, most sources) vs 1851 (National Academies account).
- UNVERIFIED — LANE3: Direct measurement that combined use makes the HANGOVER itself worse (beyond alcohol's own hangover): not found; inferred from separate literatures.

concepts.title: Acting on an unknown — what to do instead of guessing
concepts.text:
When a claim sits on shelf 3, the protective move is not to fill the gap with a guess. It is:
- Say the unknown out loud: “nobody has studied this combination.”
- Default to caution — unknown risk plus documented single-substance risk is not a wash.
- Prefer single-substance windows with screening, journaling and peer support — the only functional-support pattern with literature behind it.
- Keep the emergency lines loaded: 911 for chest pain or loss of consciousness, a sober sitter, no driving, no unsupervised medication changes (never advise stopping a prescribed antidepressant).
- Re-check fast-moving claims against today's primary source before repeating them — city resolutions and bill status move under an old stamp.

examples.title: “No cases reported, so no risk”
examples.scenario: A member argues that because nobody has documented cardiac valvulopathy from microdosing, the 5-HT2B concern can be dropped.
examples.outcome: Zero documented human cases is exactly what an unstudied chronic exposure looks like: LSD (Ki 0.98 nM) and psilocin (Ki 4.6 nM) are high-affinity 5-HT2B agonists structurally similar to known valvulopathic drugs, and the pattern that caused the fenfluramine problem was chronic exposure. The pathway stays theoretical, the case count stays zero, and cardiac screening stays the mitigation. Absence of evidence is not a green light.

examples.title: “The trials show microdosing works”
examples.scenario: Someone cites survey enthusiasm as trial-grade evidence for a functional microdosing routine.
examples.outcome: The self-blinding citizen-science trial (Szigeti 2021, n=191 — the largest placebo-controlled psychedelic trial) found improvement in both microdose and placebo arms: expectancy predicts outcome. A 2024 review still calls “placebo-only” premature, so the honest statement is that the evidence base is contested — not settled in either direction.

examples.title: “It's on the internet, so it's basically verified”
examples.scenario: A city-resolution date or bill status gets repeated in a community channel as settled fact.
examples.outcome: The Michigan legal lane refused to upgrade 11 such claims — Jackson rests on secondary trackers only, Grand Rapids details conflict, and the SB 631 / SB 499 outcomes were never confirmed. Keep the flag: “UNVERIFIED — secondary trackers only,” not “probably true.”

pitfalls: MYTH: “No data means no risk.” No data means no data — and every documented single-substance risk still applies.
Repeating a secondary-source claim until it sounds verified. A flag repeated confidently is still a flag.
Treating a zero case count as a study. Zero cases usually means nobody looked.
Never advise anyone to stop a prescribed antidepressant to make a protocol work: discontinuation syndrome is documented and can be severe — medication changes are a prescriber conversation.
exercises: Count the UNVERIFIED flags this module carries and name one that you would refuse to repeat without a primary source.
Write the three screening questions from memory, then check them against this guide.
Take a claim from shelf 3 and craft the honest two-sentence answer: what is unknown, and what caution follows from that unknown.
Look up form MC 228 and Michigan Legal Help's record-clearing page — then state, as information and not advice, what the DIY route is.

glossary.definition: A compound the liver makes when cocaine and ethanol are present together (transesterification by hCE1/hCE2). Only known psychoactive substance formed entirely inside the body; associated with an 18–25× higher sudden-death risk in a 2024 systematic review.

A compound that is pharmacologically inactive as swallowed and is converted in the body into the active molecule. Psilocybin is a prodrug: alkaline phosphatases and esterases strip its phosphate group to release psilocin.
The active metabolite of psilocybin — the molecule that crosses the blood-brain barrier and acts at 5-HT2A receptors. Every co-use interaction acts on psilocin, not on the phosphate ester.

When a co-used substance dulls the felt effect of alcohol without changing blood alcohol. Barrett 2000 found the felt effect dimmed in about 60% of psilocybin co-users and 86.7% with LSD — the reason co-use drives over-drinking.
Michigan's MCL 257.625(8): operating while visibly impaired by any detectable amount of a controlled substance, with no requirement to prove impaired driving.

A substance or mechanism that raises blood pressure. “Dual pressor stacking” is the theory that psilocin's sympathomimetic effect and cocaine's adrenergic action add cardiovascular strain — expected, never human-tested.

The inactive comparison group in a controlled trial. In microdosing research the placebo arms often improve as much as the active arms (Szigeti 2021, n=191), which is why expectancy is the central evidence-quality problem.

Michigan's expungement framework under MCL 780.621 et seq. — automatic set-asides, capped petition routes, and one shot at clearing a first-offense OWI (including drug-driving OWPD), with form MC 228 as the free self-help path.

A claim the research lanes checked and refused to upgrade: secondary source only, conflicting sources, or no source located. Flags stay attached to their claim and travel with it — 30 across this module, 11 of them in the Michigan legal lane.

The honesty spine of this guide: documented (sourced human/official data), theoretical (mechanism-reasoned, untested in humans), unstudied (no data, or data that never verified). Every claim sits on exactly one shelf.

beginner.q: When alcohol and cocaine are in the body at the same time, the liver produces which additional compound?
beginner.explain: Liver esterases (hCE1/hCE2) transesterify cocaine with ethanol into cocaethylene — the only known psychoactive substance formed entirely inside the body (source PMC8956485). Human kinetics: about 17% (±6%) conversion (PMID 14636972).

beginner.q: How much higher is the sudden-death association when cocaethylene is present, per the 2024 systematic review?
beginner.explain: The 2024 systematic review (PMC10935323) reports an 18–25× higher sudden-death association with cocaethylene present, about 21.5× with coronary disease, and cocaethylene in ~76% of cocaine-related sudden deaths in one cohort.

beginner.q: MCL 333.7214(a)(iv) — the citation this corpus corrected — names which substance?
beginner.explain: The original research brief miscited psilocybin to this section. Cocaine is MCL 333.7214(a)(iv), Schedule 2; psilocybin sits at MCL 333.7212(1)(c) (Schedule 1). Correcting citations matters because a wrong cite in a study guide misleads real cases.

beginner.q: A Michigan city passes a 'lowest enforcement priority' resolution for entheogens. What did it actually change?
options: Psilocybin became legal to possess and sell
State law was preempted for city residents
Federal law no longer applies inside the city
Nothing about legality — state and federal law still apply; only local arrest odds shift
beginner.explain: Decriminalized means deprioritized, not legal: Ann Arbor R-20-362, Detroit Proposal E and the Ferndale resolution all preserve state and federal authority. Selling or distributing is never protected.

beginner.q: In a college survey, which consequence separated simultaneous alcohol+cannabis users from everyone else after full statistical adjustment?
beginner.explain: Blackouts were the only consequence class that still differed after covariate adjustment: ~56% of simultaneous users vs ~37% concurrent-but-not-simultaneous and ~28% alcohol-only (PMC7064425).

beginner.q: Which pairing is the #1 alcohol companion among U.S. emergency-department visits involving cocaine?
beginner.explain: SAMHSA DAWN 2024: 392,510 cocaine-related ED visits, 70.2% polydrug, alcohol the top companion — the combination accounts for roughly 173,799 visits, the #1 pairing.

beginner.q: In controlled human trials, alcohol given before cannabis did what to blood THC?
options: Raised it and sped the onset of effects
beginner.explain: Lukas & Orozco 2001 (PMID 11543984) and Hartman et al. 2015 (PMC4749481, n=19 completers): ethanol before vaporized cannabis significantly raised peak THC and 11-OH-THC. The reverse also holds — cannabis dulls perceived alcohol effects, so people drink more.

beginner.q: The only systematic human data on psychedelics masking alcohol's effects (Barrett 2000, n=22) found that psilocybin co-users reported:
options: Felt alcohol effects dimmed in about 60% of co-users
beginner.explain: Barrett's retrospective interviews found 86.7% complete blockade of subjective alcohol effects with LSD and about 60% with psilocybin. Blood alcohol does not change — the felt signal does, which is why masked intoxication drives over-drinking.

beginner.q: True or False: In Michigan, one statute — MCL 257.625 — covers impaired driving by alcohol, by drugs, or by any combination of them.
beginner.explain: OWI is a single combined-substance statute: MCL 257.625(1)(a), (1)(c) and the verdict provisions (18)-(21) all carry the combination language. There is no separate 'polydrug DUI' charge with its own elements.

beginner.q: True or False: Under MCL 257.625(8), a driver can be convicted with any detectable amount of a controlled substance in the body — no proof of bad driving needed.
beginner.explain: Zero-tolerance OWPD: any amount of THC, psilocybin or cocaine in the body is enough. No impairment evidence, no bad driving, no per se threshold — buying cannabis legally does not create a driving exception.

intermediate.q: Serotonin syndrome from combining psilocybin with cocaine sits on which shelf?
options: Legal — a charging question, not a medical one
Theoretical — plausible mechanism, no documented case
Documented — shown in controlled human trials
intermediate.explain: Psilocin is a partial 5-HT2A agonist (~16% of serotonin's signaling efficacy) and does not raise intrasynaptic serotonin, which is why severe toxicity from psilocybin alone is rare. Every documented serotonin-toxicity case involves MAOIs or serotonergic medications — so the cocaine combination stays labeled theoretical.

intermediate.q: Which sentence is correctly labeled for the theory shelf?
options: 'Two pressor systems stacking is pharmacologically expected, never tested in humans'
'Psilocybin plus cocaine causes hypertensive emergencies in users' — documented
intermediate.explain: The other three each fail their own shelf: no human combination study exists for psilocybin + cocaine; the ethanol-preservation claim has zero literature support; and 'smoother' anecdotes ride on zero controlled data.

intermediate.q: The folk claim that alcohol competes with psilocin for CYP2D6 clearance is:
options: Documented in two human pharmacokinetic trials
Unsupported — ethanol runs ADH/ALDH and CYP2E1, not CYP2D6; the only published mechanism is speculative
Verified in vitro and confirmed in humans
The basis of a clinical dosing guideline
intermediate.explain: Lane 5's UNVERIFIED (theoretical) finding: ethanol is metabolized by ADH/ALDH (primary) and CYP2E1/catalase (minor). Do not present alcohol–psilocin CYP competition as fact — the honest position is 'no controlled data; one speculative MAO-inhibition hypothesis.'

intermediate.q: Chronic microdosing and 5-HT2B cardiac valvulopathy is best described as:
options: A documented epidemic in trial data
A plausible theoretical pathway with zero documented human cases
Only relevant to LSD, never to psilocybin
intermediate.explain: LSD (Ki 0.98 nM) and psilocin (Ki 4.6 nM) are high-affinity 5-HT2B agonists structurally similar to known valvulopathic drugs. The risk is preclinical and unquantified — but it matters precisely because microdosing is chronic exposure, the pattern that caused the fenfluramine problem. Cardiac screening is the mitigation.

intermediate.q: Alcohol-dependent rats show blunted psilocybin brain-network effects. What does that prove about humans?
options: Everything — the effect is documented in humans
That alcohol makes psilocybin stronger in people
Nothing directly — human blunting data are essentially absent, so the claim stays on the theory shelf
intermediate.explain: The rat default-mode-network result is documented preclinically; Barrett 2000 gives only retrospective human self-report. Species translation is an inference, not a finding.

intermediate.q: Two substances that are each independently nausea-producing are combined. The amplified nausea in alcohol + psilocybin co-use is:
options: Measured at exactly double in a human trial
intermediate.explain: Both are separately emetogenic (mushroom exposures show GI effects in 23% of U.S. poison-center misuse cases; ethanol is gastrically irritating), but no study quantifies the combination. Treat it as a risk assumption, not a measured fact.

intermediate.q: An in-vitro study found CYP2D6 metabolizes nearly 100% of psilocin — yet the human genotype study found no change in psilocin exposure. So 'CYP2D6 competition' claims should be labeled:
intermediate.explain: Lane 5 marks this MIXED: in-vitro enzyme data verified, human clinical relevance not documented. Systematic reviews still list CYP2D6/CYP3A4 as theoretical interaction pathways — which is exactly the label they deserve.

intermediate.q: In the proposed three-drug bottle, settled solids would create pour-to-pour dose differences. This hazard is:
options: Theorized from non-uniformity plus gravity — never tested, because testing it would be a protocol this guide does not provide
Impossible, because alcohol dissolves everything evenly
intermediate.explain: Extraction into a low-proof solvent is partial and non-uniform (no quantitative efficiency study exists), and solids settle. The mechanism is textbook; the specific numbers were never measured — and this guide will not be the thing that measures them.

intermediate.q: True or False: 'Alcohol blunts the microdose window through liver enzymes' is documented pharmacology.
intermediate.explain: It is folklore-adjacent. What is documented: psilocin clearance runs mainly through glucuronidation (UGT1A9/UGT1A10) plus MAO-A, and microdosers self-report avoiding alcohol on dosing days — behavior, not an enzyme mechanism.

intermediate.q: True or False: Psilocin plus cocaine stacking two independent tachycardia/hypertension systems is pharmacologically expected but has never been tested in a human combination study.
intermediate.explain: Classic psychedelics raise heart rate and blood pressure via 5-HT2A sympathomimetic action; cocaine adds direct sympathetic stimulation and vasoconstriction. Harm-reduction bodies rate the pairing 'Caution' on that basis — expectation, not measurement.

advanced.q: How many controlled human trials have deliberately co-administered alcohol with psilocybin?
advanced.explain: No human co-use trial exists for any combination in this corpus. That single fact is why the guide has three shelves instead of one.

advanced.q: The largest placebo-controlled microdosing trial (Szigeti 2021, self-blinding, n=191) found:
options: Improvement only in the microdose arm
That psychedelic trials cannot use placebo
Improvements in both microdose and placebo arms — expectancy predicts outcome
advanced.explain: The placebo problem is the core evidence-quality finding of lane 6: controlled arms do not separate, while a 2024 review still calls 'placebo-only' premature. Anyone teaching microdosing as evidence-based therapy is overstating the science.

advanced.q: How many UNVERIFIED flags does the Michigan legal lane carry?
advanced.explain: Eleven open questions the lane refused to upgrade — the Jackson resolution (secondary trackers only), conflicting Grand Rapids details, SB 631/499 outcomes, metabolite-only caselaw, implied-consent mechanics, and more. The flags ride inside the module, still labeled.

advanced.q: When a community asks for functional support and the evidence base is thin, which pattern has any literature behind it?
options: Stopping prescribed medication to 'make it work'
Single-substance windows, screening, journaling, and peer support
advanced.explain: Lane 6's beginner-safety consensus — verify dose, no co-substances in the window, sitter, no driving, journal, peer support. And never advise stopping prescribed antidepressants: discontinuation syndrome is documented and can be severe.

advanced.q: Which set matches the three-question screening screen taught by this corpus?
options: Psychosis or bipolar history? lithium or MAOI? is the schedule driven by need rather than protocol?
advanced.explain: Those three questions catch most documented contraindications: personal or family psychosis/bipolar history is a near-universal trial exclusion, lithium and MAOIs are hard contraindications, and a need-driven schedule is where misuse starts.

advanced.q: Which statement is correct about Michigan's Clean Slate expungement doorway for drug convictions?
options: Only cannabis convictions can ever be cleared
All drug convictions clear automatically on day one
Old drug convictions clear on a clock — e.g. a psilocybin possession misdemeanor after 3 years, a cocaine possession felony after 5 — and MC 228 is the free self-help form
Expungement requires an attorney and a $500 filing fee
advanced.explain: MCL 780.621 et seq. sets the caps and waiting periods; first-offense OWI (including drug-driving OWPD) gets one Clean Slate shot under MCL 780.621c, though the license record stays dirty. Michigan Legal Help's 'Clearing a Criminal Record' plus form MC 228 is the free DIY route — information, not legal advice.

advanced.q: Human cardiac valvulopathy cases arising from chronic microdosing number:
options: Zero — no clinical cases have been documented
advanced.explain: The 5-HT2B pathway is theoretical/preclinical: biologically plausible, unquantified in humans, zero documented cases. That is exactly why it belongs on shelf 3 and why screening exists as the mitigation.

advanced.q: Which of these is documented rather than theoretical?
options: Ethanol preserving psilocybin in a bottle
Serotonin syndrome from psilocybin plus cocaine
Pour-to-pour hot spots in a settled mixture
advanced.explain: That figure comes from a 2024 systematic review of human data. The other three are, respectively, theoretical (no documented case), unverified folklore, and an untested mechanistic inference — sorting those four is the whole point of the three-shelf rule.

advanced.q: True or False: There is no dedicated human sublingual pharmacokinetic study for psilocybin.
advanced.explain: Clinical psilocybin is dosed orally, and transmucosal fractions of any such dose are largely swallowed anyway — which is why the 'under the tongue' promise in the tincture question has no human data behind it.

advanced.q: True or False: Published literature validates ethanol as a psilocin preservative.
advanced.explain: The claim is UNVERIFIED and the chemistry argues against it: psilocin oxidizes to blue quinoid oligomers and is unstable even in whole blood. 'Booze preserves it' is folklore with no located supporting study.
